newsitem.title: UK: Thefts at SA gold mines may have peaked-GFMS chief.
newsitem.headline: Thefts at SA gold mines may have peaked-GFMS chief.

text.p: Thefts from South Africa's gold mines have probably peaked now that security has been beefed up at the facilities, according to Stewart Murray, chief executive of consultant Gold Fields Mineral Services Ltd (GFMS).
"It has been there for some time but it is not a major factor in the decline of South African gold production," Murray said at the launch of his Gold 1997 survey of the industry.
According to the survey South Africa, by far the largest producer of gold, mined 496 tonnes last year, the first time it has produced less than 500 tonnes since 1956.
In 1993, the country produced 619.50 tonnes of gold according to the GFMS survey.
He said it was impossible to put a figure on the amount involved but the feeling was there was less gold lost last year than in 1995.
"There is a huge range of figures for the amount involved," he said.
Murray said it was thought initially that thefts only occurred at a mine's smelter unit where gold is refined but security checks showed that thefts also occurred from the metallurgical plant.
Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd chief executive Alan Wright said, "You push the security further and further back so that people are caught with lower and lower levels of (gold) concentrates."
He said a possible new source of gold theft was mud being carried up from underground drains that would previously have been pumped to the surface.
"There is a view that about 30 tonnes a year of stolen gold is leaving the country. I think that is not physically possible," Wright said.
